Charter

Telling stories with dignity

A story is a gift entrusted to us. These are the commitments we and our volunteers make every time we tell someone’s life.

  1. 1

    Hope before need

    We tell the moment things turn around, not the misery. No image or phrase that humiliates, invites pity, or reduces a person to their situation.

  2. 2

    First names, never precise places

    First name only — often changed. Never a last name, address, school or place that could identify someone.

  3. 3

    Written, revocable consent

    Each person (or their parent or guardian) consents in writing, can read their story before it is published, and can ask us to remove it at any time.

  4. 4

    Children protected first

    No close-up portraits of children, and none in distress. Children appear in groups, from behind, through their hands, or as illustrations. No direct correspondence with a child.

  5. 5

    The person’s own voice

    As much as possible, people tell their own story in their own words. We always say who is telling it.

  6. 6

    The truth, untouched

    We invent no figures and no testimonies. An illustrative photo is labelled as such. A sample is marked as a sample.

La Paix du Cœur
Montréal · 2026

Think we have fallen short of this charter? Write to us: we will correct it quickly. lapaixducoeur.ca@gmail.com

A Christian association serving orphans, widows, people in need and the homeless — Montréal, since 2014.
